messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

yo! friend works, but i need your actual name to find you roles that don't suck

what's your full name?
Anuj
anuj... solid name. where you working these days?
I am working at a Series-A funded startup in construction tech space called parspec
no you should look for anuj kumar, engineering @parspec
ah got it! found anuj kumar - engineering at parspec, ex-paytm, iiitd '22. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/anuj-kumar-b90113175

construction tech at parspec... digitizing an industry that still runs on excel and handshakes. respect.

found anuj chandarana - head of hr, google canada. this you? https://ca.linkedin.com/in/anuj-chandarana-66a1a46
correct!

iiitd '22 to paytm to parspec... from fintech payments to construction tech. that's a proper pivot from moving money to moving dirt. what made you jump from the paytm machine to building for contractors?

makes sense. frontend at paytm was probably just another cog in the machine, but at parspec you actually get to shape the product. startup ownership hits different when your code directly impacts whether contractors get paid or not.

how long you been working total?
exactly 3.5 yoe now

3.5 years... solid mid-level territory. not fresh enough to be exploited, not senior enough to be ignored. perfect timing to level up.

what kind of role you looking for next?

I have an expertise in react, typescript. mostly worked with these two. Goes without saying I am equally good at html, css, js. 
I have worked with material ui, graphql, redux etc. 
So preferably a role where all these skills come handy. 
It is hard for me to work 5 days from office, so preferably 2-3 a week office/hybrid (or even remote) work situation would be ideal.

react, typescript, graphql... you've got the modern frontend stack locked down. material ui means you actually care about making things look good, not just functional.

2-3 days office is the sweet spot - enough face time to not be forgotten, enough home time to actually code without distractions.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
bangalore and open to remote, won't prefer other cities at the moment
3.5 years experience + frontend engineering + bangalore/remote + hybrid setup... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
absolutely

absolutely
  Thanks looking forward to it

yooo anuj! welcome to the tal network legend 🔥

you're officially in the system. frontend roles that actually matter are about to slide into your dm's. no more scrolling through naukri wondering if that "urgent requirement" is legit.

parspec to something bigger... let's see what we can cook up for you
Hi
Hi
what's good anuj? how's the parspec life treating you?
Good man
nice. so what's making you want to leave? just growth or something else?
Yeah it is really the lack of variety and depth in the work. I have just been shipping features one after the other without getting any opportunity to get deeper or learn something new

feature factory mode... that's the startup trap. you get ownership but then it's just churning out features without the technical depth.

what kind of deeper work you looking for? architecture stuff, performance, new tech?
Yeah preferbaly a good mix of architecture and enhancing performance. Not necessarily new tech but i wont mind that either

got it. architecture + performance focus. that's the sweet spot for 3-4 YOE frontend engineers who want to level up.

what's your current comp? and what would make you actually move?
I am at 27 base + 10% variable + some esops. I am expecting a hike in 2 months that will take me around 32-33 base. So I would prefer upwards of 40/42 base ideally

40-42 base for 3.5 YOE frontend in this market... ambitious but not impossible if you find the right company. especially with that startup experience.

you're basically looking at senior roles at series B+ startups or mid-level at bigger companies. makes sense.

any companies you'd never work for?
Not really

cool. you're locked in.

i'll slide roles when they're good... btw what's making you want to leave parspec anyway? just the lack of depth or something else?
Yeah thats it

got it. feature factory burnout is real.

i'll keep an eye out for roles that actually give you that architecture + performance work. something that makes you think instead of just shipping.

you're in the system now. something good comes up, you'll be the first to know.

hey, saw a react/typescript role at Virtuos

they're building a DXP platform with AI tools like Cursor and Copilot

it's in gurgaon though, not bangalore. remote flexibility mentioned

service-based companies are a different game - you're building for clients, not users. less ownership, more scope creep.

i'll filter for product companies only from now on.

some of these listings are wild. i'll filter out anything that's not senior-level with proper comp.

you're looking at 40+ base, senior scope, product company. i'll be more selective with what i share.

hey, happy monday - if it’s not, we’ll work together on making it happen soon :)
how’s the week looking? what would you like me to focus on this week with the search?
